rowwise_role: It is the only and primary inferential result; the report headlines t = 5.183, df = 118, p = 9.13e-07, n = 120 worms.

label: NEGATIVE
evidence: reduce_to_one_value_per_rider() collapses each rider's five sprints to one mean before any test, and the primary Welch t-test runs on those 18 rider-level values with the report stating explicitly "The sample size is 9 riders in the supplement group and 9 in the placebo group... It is not 90."
rowwise_role: No row-level (90-sprint) test is computed anywhere in analysis.py; the report only mentions in prose that such a test would have given a smaller and wrong p-value.

primary_entered: every raw row, which here is also one value per unit (24 bogs, 24 rows)
label: NEGATIVE
evidence: The CSV has 24 rows and 24 distinct bog_id values, and check_design() raises an error unless n_rows equals n_units, so the row-level Welch t-test is by construction a test on the 24 independent bogs with no repeated measurement to pool.
rowwise_role: It is the primary and valid test, since a row is a unit; Student's t, Mann-Whitney, Levene and Shapiro-Wilk are labelled secondary sensitivity checks.

primary_entered: a model with unit-level random effects (linear mixed model, random intercept per bird, fitted on all 168 rows)
stated_N: 14 birds, 168 bouts; the primary effect is -0.500 s, Wald z = -2.33, p = 0.020
label: NEGATIVE
evidence: primary_mixed_model() fits bout_duration_s ~ noise_condition + (1 | bird_id) by REML as the stated primary inference, and the plain 168-row t-test is printed inside secondary_checks() under the heading "SECONDARY SENSITIVITY CHECKS (not the inferential result)" with an explicit pseudoreplication warning.
rowwise_role: Check S1, explicitly labelled a sensitivity check and "not valid for the study question"; the report calls it pseudoreplication and contrasts its p = 1.4e-09 against the honest p = 0.020.

primary_entered: one value per unit read from a separate pre-summarized file (mean_nitrate_mg_per_l, one row per well)
source_file: well_nitrate_summary.csv (the 132-row nitrate_monitoring_log.csv is used descriptively only)
label: NEGATIVE
evidence: compare_groups() takes only the summary frame and is documented "Unit of analysis: the well. Sample size = number of wells per group", while the module docstring states the raw log "is used for DESCRIPTIVE purposes only" because 132 rows would be pseudoreplication.
rowwise_role: No two-sample test is run on the 132 raw rows; describe_raw() only computes counts, means and SDs from them, and the report says "No test is run on this file."

primary_entered: a cluster-aware resampling (10,000-replicate bootstrap drawing whole mounds with replacement, stratified by block, all 8 cores travelling with their mound)
stated_N: 14 mounds (7 per block), 112 cores; effect -0.0516, 95% CI [-0.0863, -0.0177], bootstrap p = 0.0029
label: NEGATIVE
evidence: cluster_bootstrap() resamples whole mounds rather than cores for both the interval and the null p-value, and the report states "The dependence-aware cluster bootstrap is the study's conclusion" while the 112-row Welch t-test sits under the heading "ILLUSTRATIVE CONTRAST ONLY -- NOT A VALID INFERENCE FOR THIS DESIGN".
rowwise_role: An illustrative contrast only, printed with an explicit warning that it claims 112 independent units when the study has 14 and that its standard error is understated by a factor of about 2.3.
